theorem primeArch_twoEisenstein_plus (p : Polynomial ℤ) (d N : ℕ)
    (hpd : p.natDegree < d) :
    (Polynomial.X ^ d + Polynomial.C 2 +
      Polynomial.C (4 * (N : ℤ)) * p).IsEisensteinAt primeArchTwoEisensteinIdeal
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem primeArch_twoEisenstein_plus (p : Polynomial ℤ) (d N : ℕ)
    (hpd : p.natDegree < d) :
    (Polynomial.X ^ d + Polynomial.C 2 +
      Polynomial.C (4 * (N : ℤ)) * p).IsEisensteinAt primeArchTwoEisensteinIdeal
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let lower : Polynomial ℤ := Polynomial.C 2 + Polynomial.C (4 * (N : ℤ)) * p
  have hd : 0 < d := lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.zero_le _) hpd
  have hlowNat : lower.natDegree < d := by
    dsimp only [lower]
    apply lt_of_le_of_lt (Polynomial.natDegree_add_le _ _)
    rw [max_lt_iff]
    constructor
    · simpa using hd
    · exact lt_of_le_of_lt (Polynomial.natDegree_C_mul_le _ _) hpd
  have hlowDegree : lower.degree < (d : WithBot ℕ) := by
    by_cases hzero : lower = 0
    · simp [hzero]
    · exact (Polynomial.natDegree_lt_iff_degree_lt hzero).mp hlowNat
  have hmonic : (Polynomial.X ^ d + lower).Monic :=
    Polynomial.monic_X_pow_add hlowDegree
  have hne : primeArchTwoEisensteinIdeal ≠ ⊤ := by
    dsimp only [primeArchTwoEisensteinIdeal]
    exact (Ideal.span_singleton_prime (by norm_num : (2 : ℤ) ≠ 0)).mpr (by norm_num) |>.ne_top
  have hsumDegree : (Polynomial.X ^ d + lower).natDegree = d := by
    have hlow' : lower.natDegree <
        ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial ℤ) ^ d).natDegree := by
      simpa only [Polynomial.natDegree_X_pow] using hlowNat
    rw [Polynomial.natDegree_add_eq_left_of_natDegree_lt hlow',
      Polynomial.natDegree_X_pow]
  have hmem : ∀ {n}, n < (Polynomial.X ^ d + lower).natDegree →
      (Polynomial.X ^ d + lower).coeff n ∈ primeArchTwoEisensteinIdeal := by
    intro n hn
    rw [hsumDegree] at hn
    dsimp only [primeArchTwoEisensteinIdeal]
    rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton]
    have hnd : n ≠ d := Nat.ne_of_lt hn
    dsimp only [lower]
    simp only [Polynomial.coeff_add, Polynomial.coeff_X_pow, if_neg hnd,
      zero_add, Polynomial.coeff_C_mul]
    by_cases hn0 : n = 0
    · subst n
      simp only [Polynomial.coeff_C_zero]
      exact dvd_add (by norm_num) ⟨2 * (N : ℤ) * p.coeff 0, by ring⟩
    · rw [Polynomial.coeff_C, if_neg hn0, zero_add]
      exact ⟨2 * (N : ℤ) * p.coeff n, by ring⟩
  have hnotMem :
      (Polynomial.X ^ d + lower).coeff 0 ∉ primeArchTwoEisensteinIdeal ^ 2 := by
    dsimp only [primeArchTwoEisensteinIdeal]
    rw [Ideal.span_singleton_pow, Ideal.mem_span_singleton]
    simp only [pow_two]
    dsimp only [lower]
    simp only [Polynomial.coeff_add, Polynomial.coeff_X_pow,
      if_neg (Nat.ne_of_lt hd), zero_add, Polynomial.coeff_C_zero,
      Polynomial.coeff_C_mul]
    intro hfour
    have hterm : ((2 : ℤ) * 2) ∣ 4 * (N : ℤ) * p.coeff 0 := by
      refine ⟨(N : ℤ) * p.coeff 0, ?_⟩
      ring
    have hdiff := dvd_sub hfour hterm
    have : ((2 : ℤ) * 2) ∣ 2 := by
      simpa only [add_sub_cancel_right] using hdiff
    norm_num at this
  simpa only [lower, add_assoc] using
    hmonic.isEisensteinAt_of_mem_of_notMem hne hmem hnotMem

private theorem isEisensteinAt_map_ringEquiv
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (e : R ≃+* S) {f : Polynomial R} {I : Ideal R}
    (hf : f.IsEisensteinAt I) :
    (f.map e).IsEisensteinAt (I.map e)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hmem_iff (J : Ideal R) (x : R) :
      e.toRingHom x ∈ J.map e.toRingHom ↔ x ∈ J := by
    constructor
    · intro hx
      rcases
          (Ideal.mem_map_iff_of_surjective e.toRingHom e.surjective).1 hx with
        ⟨y, hy, hey⟩
      exact e.injective hey ▸ hy
    · exact Ideal.mem_map_of_mem e.toRingHom
  constructor
  · rw [Polynomial.leadingCoeff_map_of_injective e.injective]
    change e.toRingHom f.leadingCoeff ∉ I.map e.toRingHom
    rw [hmem_iff I]
    exact hf.leading
  · intro i hi
    rw [Polynomial.natDegree_map_eq_of_injective e.injective] at hi
    rw [Polynomial.coeff_map]
    change e.toRingHom (f.coeff i) ∈ I.map e.toRingHom
    rw [hmem_iff I]
    exact hf.mem hi
  · rw [Polynomial.coeff_map, ← Ideal.map_pow]
    change e.toRingHom (f.coeff 0) ∉ (I ^ 2).map e.toRingHom
    rw [hmem_iff (I ^ 2)]
    exact hf.notMem

source_arguments.statement:
theorem mem_adjoin_of_smul_prime_smul_of_minpoly_isEisensteinAt {B : PowerBasis K L}
    (hp : Prime p) (hBint : IsIntegral R B.gen) {z : L} (hzint : IsIntegral R z)
    (hz : p • z ∈ adjoin R ({B.gen} : Set L)) (hei : (minpoly R B.gen).IsEisensteinAt 𝓟) :
    z ∈ adjoin R ({B.gen} : Set L)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem mem_adjoin_of_smul_prime_smul_of_minpoly_isEisensteinAt {B : PowerBasis K L}
    (hp : Prime p) (hBint : IsIntegral R B.gen) {z : L} (hzint : IsIntegral R z)
    (hz : p • z ∈ adjoin R ({B.gen} : Set L)) (hei : (minpoly R B.gen).IsEisensteinAt 𝓟) :
    z ∈ adjoin R ({B.gen} : Set L)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  -- First define some abbreviations.
  have hndiv : ¬p ^ 2 ∣ (minpoly R B.gen).coeff 0 := fun h =>
    hei.notMem ((span_singleton_pow p 2).symm ▸ Ideal.mem_span_singleton.2 h)
  have := B.finite
  set P := minpoly R B.gen with hP
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero B.dim_pos.ne'
  have : Module.IsTorsionFree R L := .trans_faithfulSMul R K L
  let _ := P.map (algebraMap R L)
  -- There is a polynomial `Q` such that `p • z = aeval B.gen Q`. We can assume that
  -- `Q.degree < P.degree` and `Q ≠ 0`.
  rw [adjoin_singleton_eq_range_aeval] at hz
  obtain ⟨Q₁, hQ⟩ := hz
  set Q := Q₁ %ₘ P with hQ₁
  replace hQ : aeval B.gen Q = p • z := by simpa [hQ₁, hP] using hQ
  by_cases hQzero : Q = 0
  · simp only [hQzero, Algebra.smul_def, zero_eq_mul, aeval_zero] at hQ
    rcases hQ with H | H₁
    · have : Function.Injective (algebraMap R L) := by
        rw [algebraMap_eq R K L]
        exact (algebraMap K L).injective.comp (IsFractionRing.injective R K)
      exfalso
      exact hp.ne_zero ((injective_iff_map_eq_zero _).1 this _ H)
    · rw [H₁]
      exact Subalgebra.zero_mem _
  -- It is enough to prove that all coefficients of `Q` are divisible by `p`, by induction.
  -- The base case is `dvd_coeff_zero_of_aeval_eq_prime_smul_of_minpoly_isEisensteinAt`.
  refine mem_adjoin_of_dvd_coeff_of_dvd_aeval hp.ne_zero (fun i => ?_) hQ
  induction i using Nat.case_strong_induction_on with
  | hz =>
    intro
    exact dvd_coeff_zero_of_aeval_eq_prime_smul_of_minpoly_isEisensteinAt hp hBint hQ hzint hei
  | hi j hind =>
    intro hj
    convert! hp.dvd_of_pow_dvd_pow_mul_pow_of_square_not_dvd (n := n) _ hndiv
    -- Two technical results we will need about `P.natDegree` and `Q.natDegree`.
    have H := degree_modByMonic_lt Q₁ (minpoly.monic hBint)
    rw [← hQ₁, ← hP] at H
    replace H := Nat.lt_iff_add_one_le.1
      (lt_of_lt_of_le
        (lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.lt_iff_add_one_le.1 (Nat.lt_of_succ_lt_succ (mem_range.1 hj)))
          (lt_succ_self _)) (Nat.lt_iff_add_one_le.1 ((natDegree_lt_natDegree_iff hQzero).2 H)))
    have Hj : Q.natDegree + 1 = j + 1 + (Q.natDegree - j) := by
      rw [← add_comm 1, ← add_comm 1, add_assoc, add_right_inj,
        ← Nat.add_sub_assoc (Nat.lt_of_succ_lt_succ (mem_range.1 hj)).le, add_comm,
        Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    -- By induction hypothesis we can find `g : ℕ → R` such that
    -- `k ∈ range (j + 1) → Q.coeff k • B.gen ^ k = (algebraMap R L) p * g k • B.gen ^ k`-
    choose! g hg using hind
    replace hg : ∀ k ∈ range (j + 1), Q.coeff k • B.gen ^ k =
        algebraMap R L p * g k • B.gen ^ k := by
      intro k hk
      rw [hg k (mem_range_succ_iff.1 hk)
        (mem_range_succ_iff.2
          (le_trans (mem_range_succ_iff.1 hk) (succ_le_iff.1 (mem_range_succ_iff.1 hj)).le)),
        Algebra.smul_def, Algebra.smul_def, map_mul, mul_assoc]
    -- Since `minpoly R B.gen` is Eisenstein, we can find `f : ℕ → L` such that
    -- `(map (algebraMap R L) (minpoly R B.gen)).nat_degree ≤ i` implies `f i ∈ R[B.gen]`
    -- and `(algebraMap R L) p * f i = B.gen ^ i`. We will also need `hf₁`, a reformulation of this
    -- property.
    choose! f hf using
      IsWeaklyEisensteinAt.exists_mem_adjoin_mul_eq_pow_natDegree_le (minpoly.aeval R B.gen)
        (minpoly.monic hBint) hei.isWeaklyEisensteinAt
    have hf₁ : ∀ k ∈ (range (Q.natDegree - j)).erase 0,
        Q.coeff (j + 1 + k) • B.gen ^ (j + 1 + k) * B.gen ^ (P.natDegree - (j + 2)) =
        (algebraMap R L) p * Q.coeff (j + 1 + k) • f (k + P.natDegree - 1) := by
      intro k hk
      rw [smul_mul_assoc, ← pow_add, ← Nat.add_sub_assoc H, add_comm (j + 1) 1,
        add_assoc (j + 1), add_comm _ (k + P.natDegree), Nat.add_sub_add_right,
        ← (hf (k + P.natDegree - 1) _).2, mul_smul_comm]
      rw [(minpoly.monic hBint).natDegree_map, add_comm, Nat.add_sub_assoc, le_add_iff_nonneg_right]
      · exact Nat.zero_le _
      · refine one_le_iff_ne_zero.2 fun h => ?_
        rw [h] at hk
        simp at hk
    -- The Eisenstein condition shows that `p` divides `Q.coeff j`
    -- if `p^n.succ` divides the following multiple of `Q.coeff (succ j)^n.succ`:
    suffices
        p ^ n.succ ∣ Q.coeff (succ j) ^ n.succ *
          (minpoly R B.gen).coeff 0 ^ (succ j + (P.natDegree - (j + 2))) by

```text
    Monic(P) -> EisensteinAt(2,P) -> degree(P) in D ->
    Residual(tail(P)) ->
```

```text
Residual(tail(P)),
Var_PG(tail(P)) < 0.                                            (E2)
```

```text
not RH -> Finite(N \\ BadDeg).                                  (E2c)
```

degree carries a structured negative centered witness.

## Statement

The Wigner--Eisenstein calculation for the Hedenmalm theta source produces the conjugate
fourth-order dilation factors

```text
((D-1/2)^2+b^2)((D+1/2)^2+b^2).
```

At logarithmic Fourier frequency `tau`, their scalar symbol is

```text
p_b(tau)=|(i tau-1/2)^2+b^2|^2
        =(b^2+1/4-tau^2)^2+tau^2.                        (1)
```

Its exact lower edge is

```text
m(b)= (b^2+1/4)^2,  |b|<=1/2,
      b^2,            |b|>1/2.                           (2)
```

For every real `b,tau`,

```text
0<m(b)<=p_b(tau),                                        (3)
```

and equality is attained at

```text
tau=0,                         |b|<=1/2,
tau=+-sqrt(b^2-1/4),           |b|>1/2.                  (4)
```

The same module identifies the elementary centered completion weight

```text
q_b(a)=|((a+i b)^2-1/4)|^2
      =((a-1/2)^2+b^2)((a+1/2)^2+b^2)                    (4a)
```

and proves

```text
q_b'(a)=4a(a^2+b^2-1/4).                                  (4b)
```

Thus for `a>0` the completion points toward the Euler half-plane exactly outside the radius-`1/2`
central disk, and points oppositely inside it.

The ordered-pair polynomial in the theta Wigner expansion is also formalized:

```text
(c^2 e^(4v)-3c e^(2v))(c^2 e^(-4v)-3c e^(-2v))
 =c^4-6c^3 cosh(2v)+9c^2.                                (4c)
```

This is the algebraic collapse that removes the theta-index ratio from the Bessel kernel; the
ratio survives only in the separate divisor-character phase.

## Proof

Equation `(1)` is direct complex algebra.  Put `u=tau^2` and `A=b^2+1/4`.  Then

```text
p_b(tau)=(A-u)^2+u.
```

If `b^2<=1/4`,

```text
p_b(tau)-A^2
 =u(u+1/2-2b^2)>=0.                                     (5)
```

If `b^2>1/4`,

```text
p_b(tau)-b^2
 =(u-(b^2-1/4))^2>=0.                                   (6)
```

Equations `(4)` follow by equality in `(5)` and `(6)`.

The archimedean differential operator in the Wigner--Eisenstein orientation current has no null
frequency and no negative spectral direction.  Its inverse is bounded on each fixed Eisenstein
frequency fiber by `m(b)^(-1)` at the scalar-symbol level.

More exactly, for every `R>=0`,

```text

 iff |tau^2-(b^2-1/4)|<=R.                               (7)
```

Thus every bounded-excess state is forced into a quantified neighborhood of the characteristic
shell; this is not an asymptotic heuristic.

This does not orient the Xi Bezoutian.  The remaining sign lies in the mixed pairing of this


/-- Literal square-root-normalized Eisenstein Bessel tail. -/
def d4BMCompletedEisensteinSqrtPolynomialBesselJetTail
    (u nu : ℂ) (indexDegree heightDegree : ℕ) (Y : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  ∑' N : ℕ,
    (d4BMCompletedEisensteinWhittakerCoefficient u ⟨N + 1, by omega⟩ *
      ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ indexDegree) *
      (Real.sqrt Y : ℂ) * (Y : ℂ) ^ heightDegree *
      GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.modifiedBesselKOrder
        (2 * Real.pi * ((N : ℝ) + 1) * Y) nu

/-- On the positive cusp, square-root normalization factors through the next integer-height jet. -/
theorem d4BM_sqrtPolynomialBesselJetTail_eq_ratio_mul
    (u nu : ℂ) (indexDegree heightDegree : ℕ) {Y : ℝ} (hY : 0 < Y) :
    d4BMCompletedEisensteinSqrtPolynomialBesselJetTail
        u nu indexDegree heightDegree Y =
      ((Real.sqrt Y / Y : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        d4BMCompletedEisensteinPolynomialBesselJetTail
          u nu indexDegree (heightDegree + 1) Y := by
  rw [d4BMCompletedEisensteinSqrtPolynomialBesselJetTail,
    d4BMCompletedEisensteinPolynomialBesselJetTail, ← tsum_mul_left]
  apply tsum_congr
  intro N
  rw [pow_succ]
  push_cast
  field_simp [hY.ne']

/-- The literal square-root normalization divided by height tends to zero at the cusp. -/
theorem d4BM_tendsto_sqrt_div_self_atTop_zero :
    Tendsto (fun Y : ℝ => Real.sqrt Y / Y) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  have hinv : Tendsto (fun Y : ℝ => (Real.sqrt Y)⁻¹) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
    tendsto_inv_atTop_zero.comp Real.tendsto_sqrt_atTop
  apply hinv.congr'
  filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop (0 : ℝ)] with Y hY
  have hsqrt : Real.sqrt Y ≠ 0 := (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hY).ne'
  rw [div_eq_mul_inv]
  field_simp [hsqrt, hY.ne']
  exact (Real.sq_sqrt hY.le).symm

/-- Every literal square-root-normalized polynomial-index Eisenstein Whittaker tail vanishes. -/
theorem tendsto_d4BMCompletedEisensteinSqrtPolynomialBesselJetTail_atTop_zero
    (u nu : ℂ) (indexDegree heightDegree : ℕ) :
    Tendsto
      (d4BMCompletedEisensteinSqrtPolynomialBesselJetTail
        u nu indexDegree heightDegree) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  have hratio : Tendsto (fun Y : ℝ => ((Real.sqrt Y / Y : ℝ) : ℂ)) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
    Complex.continuous_ofReal.continuousAt.tendsto.comp d4BM_tendsto_sqrt_div_self_atTop_zero
  have htail := tendsto_d4BMCompletedEisensteinPolynomialBesselJetTail_atTop_zero
    u nu indexDegree (heightDegree + 1)
  have hprod := hratio.mul htail
  simp only [mul_zero] at hprod
  apply hprod.congr'
  filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop (0 : ℝ)] with Y hY
  exact (d4BM_sqrtPolynomialBesselJetTail_eq_ratio_mul
    u nu indexDegree heightDegree hY).symm

section AdditiveDivisorCap

/-- **The additive-divisor route, fed its conjecturally exact input, caps at `1/8`.**
Vinogradov's conjectural pointwise size `Δ_k(x,h) ≪ x^{1-1/k+ε}` together with square-root
cancellation in the shift average is the input `(a,b) = (1/2, 1-1/k)`.  For every `k ≥ 4` the
resulting pointwise exponent `transferBound k (1/2) (1-1/k) / (2k)` is **exactly `1/8`** — a plateau
across all `k ≥ 4`, not a coincidence at one index. -/
theorem vinogradov_cap {k : ℝ} (hk : 4 ≤ k) :
    transferBound k (1/2) (1 - 1/k) / (2*k) = 1/8 := by
  have hk0 : (0:ℝ) < k := by linarith
  rw [transferBound_vinogradov hk0, max_eq_right (by linarith : (0:ℝ) ≤ k/4 - 1)]
  field_simp
  ring

/-- Below `k = 4` the same input gives `1/(2k) ≥ 1/8`, so the minimum over all `k > 0` is attained
at `k = 4` and equals `1/8`. -/
theorem vinogradov_cap_below {k : ℝ} (hk : 0 < k) (hk4 : k ≤ 4) :
    transferBound k (1/2) (1 - 1/k) / (2*k) = 1/(2*k) ∧ 1/8 ≤ 1/(2*k) := by
  constructor
  · rw [transferBound_vinogradov hk, max_eq_left (by linarith : k/4 - 1 ≤ 0)]
    ring
  · rw [div_le_div_iff₀ (by norm_num) (by linarith)]
    linarith

/-- **Consequence.**  Even a complete solution of the `k`-ary additive divisor problem, at its
conjecturally exact strength and for every `k`, yields only `μ(1/2) ≤ 1/8` through the shift-average
transfer — never the Lindelöf hypothesis.  The transfer is irreducibly lossy: the true moment
exponent is `m(k) = 1`, while the transfer delivers `m(k) ≤ k/4` for `k ≥ 4`. -/

    transferBound 4 (1/2) (1 - 1/4) / (2*(4:ℝ)) = 1/8 ∧
      transferBound 6 (1/2) (1 - 1/6) / (2*(6:ℝ)) = 1/8 ∧
      transferBound 12 (1/2) (1 - 1/12) / (2*(12:ℝ)) = 1/8 := by
  refine ⟨vinogradov_cap (by norm_num), vinogradov_cap (by norm_num),
    vinogradov_cap (by norm_num)⟩

/-- The **conspiracy exponent**.  The off-diagonal of the `2k`-th moment is
`∑_h (D_k(M,h)/M) K(h)` with `K(h) ≪ min(T, M/h)`; note the normalising `1/M`.  Modelling the errors

`∑_{h≤M} K(h)^2 ≍ 2MT`, the predicted error is

/-!
# Finite weighted-barycentric readers

An exact weighted-barycentric packet reader is the projectivization of an additive marked
current.  Multiplication by the total mass recovers that current, so a positive barycentric
normalization preserves scalar zero loci and signs.  This is the reusable algebraic classification
needed by the edge-marked Gamma--Jacobi reader.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- Total mass of a finite marked packet. -/
def finiteBarycentricTotalMass
    {E : Type*} (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ e ∈ edges, mass e

/-- Additive mass-weighted current carried by a finite marked packet. -/
def finiteBarycentricCurrent
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V]
    (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V) : V :=
  ∑ e ∈ edges, mass e • value e

/-- Normalized weighted-barycentric reader of a finite marked packet. -/
def finiteBarycentricReader
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V]
    (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V) : V :=
  (finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass)⁻¹ •
    finiteBarycentricCurrent edges mass value

/-- **Dehomogenization law.**  Multiplication by nonzero total mass recovers the additive marked
current exactly. -/
theorem finiteBarycentricTotalMass_smul_reader
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V]
    (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V)
    (htotal : finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass ≠ 0) :
    finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass •
        finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value =
      finiteBarycentricCurrent edges mass value := by
  rw [finiteBarycentricReader, smul_smul,
    mul_inv_cancel₀ htotal, one_smul]

/-- Exact converse classification: a proposed packet value is the barycentric reader exactly
when its mass-weighted lift is the additive marked current. -/
theorem finiteBarycentricReader_eq_iff_totalMass_smul_eq_current
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V]
    (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V) (v : V)
    (htotal : finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass ≠ 0) :
    finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value = v ↔
      finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass • v =
        finiteBarycentricCurrent edges mass value := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    rw [← h]
    exact finiteBarycentricTotalMass_smul_reader edges mass value htotal
  · intro h
    rw [finiteBarycentricReader, ← h, smul_smul,
      inv_mul_cancel₀ htotal, one_smul]

/-- A nonzero normalization cannot create or remove a zero of the additive current. -/
theorem finiteBarycentricReader_eq_zero_iff_current_eq_zero
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V]
    (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V)
    (htotal : finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass ≠ 0) :
    finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value = 0 ↔
      finiteBarycentricCurrent edges mass value = 0 := by
  rw [finiteBarycentricReader]
  exact smul_eq_zero.trans (or_iff_right (inv_ne_zero htotal))

/-- Linear observation commutes with finite barycentric normalization. -/
theorem LinearMap.map_finiteBarycentricReader
    {E V W : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V]
    [AddCommMonoid W] [Module ℝ W]
    (L : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V) :
    L (finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value) =
      finiteBarycentricReader edges mass (fun e => L (value e)) := by
  simp only [finiteBarycentricReader, finiteBarycentricCurrent,
    map_smul, map_sum]

/-- Negating every marked value negates the packet reader. -/
theorem finiteBarycentricReader_neg
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V]
    (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V) :
    finiteBarycentricReader edges mass (fun e => -value e) =
      -finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value := by
  simp [finiteBarycentricReader, finiteBarycentricCurrent,
    smul_neg, Finset.sum_neg_distrib]

/-- Positive normalization preserves strict positivity of a real additive current. -/
theorem finiteBarycentricReader_pos_iff_current_pos
    {E : Type*} (edges : Finset E) (mass value : E → ℝ)
    (htotal : 0 < finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass) :
    0 < finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value ↔
      0 < finiteBarycentricCurrent edges mass value := by
  rw [finiteBarycentricReader]
  exact smul_pos_iff_of_pos_left (inv_pos.mpr htotal)

/-- Positive normalization preserves strict negativity of a real additive current. -/
theorem finiteBarycentricReader_neg_iff_current_neg
    {E : Type*} (edges : Finset E) (mass value : E → ℝ)
    (htotal : 0 < finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass) :
    finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value < 0 ↔
      finiteBarycentricCurrent edges mass value < 0 := by
  rw [finiteBarycentricReader]

/-- Moment-error exponent predicted by the independent-signs model from a correlation size exponent
`s`, at the balanced length `M = T^{k/2}`. -/
noncomputable def modelPrediction (k s : ℝ) : ℝ := 1/2 + k * (s - 1/2) / 2

/-- **The size exponent is uniquely determined by the model's verified output.** -/
theorem modelPrediction_eq_quarter_iff {k s : ℝ} (hk : 0 < k) :
    modelPrediction k s = k/4 ↔ s = 1 - 1/k := by
  unfold modelPrediction
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hk' : k ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hk
    field_simp at h ⊢
    nlinarith [h]
  · intro h
    subst h
    have hk' : k ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hk
    field_simp
    ring

/-- At `k = 1` the forced size is `0`: the correlation error for `d₁ ≡ 1` is bounded, and the model
returns `E₁ ≍ T^{1/4}` — the proved value. -/
theorem forcedSize_one : modelPrediction 1 (1 - 1/1) = 1/4 := by
  unfold modelPrediction; norm_num

/-- At `k = 2` the forced size is `1/2`, where Ivić's and Conrey–Gonek's proposals coincide, and the
model returns `E₂ ≍ T^{1/2}` — the proved value. -/
theorem forcedSize_two : modelPrediction 2 (1 - 1/2) = 1/2 := by
  unfold modelPrediction; norm_num

/-- **Conrey–Gonek's constant meets the model only at `k = 2`.**  Taking `s = 1/2` for every `k`
would predict `E_k ≍ T^{1/2}` at every index, which is the correct value only at `k = 2`. -/
theorem conreyGonek_size_fits_only_at_two {k : ℝ} (hk : 0 < k) :
    modelPrediction k (1/2) = k/4 ↔ k = 2 := by
  rw [modelPrediction_eq_quarter_iff hk]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hk' : k ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hk
    field_simp at h
    linarith
  · rintro rfl; norm_num

/-- The constant size predicts `T^{1/2}` at every index — in particular at `k = 1`, where the proved
value is `T^{1/4}`. -/
theorem conreyGonek_size_prediction (k : ℝ) : modelPrediction k (1/2) = 1/2 := by
  unfold modelPrediction; norm_num

/-- **The consequence.**  The forced size is Ivić's, and Ivić's size delivers `m(k) = 1` only for
`k ≤ 3`; the additive-divisor route with it is therefore capped.  This is the model's own verdict on
the dichotomy it was built to describe. -/
theorem model_forces_ivic_size {k : ℝ} (hk : 0 < k) :
    (modelPrediction k (ivicSize k) = k/4) ∧
    (transferBound k 1 (ivicSize k) = 1 ↔ k ≤ 3) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ivic_gives_one_iff hk⟩
  rw [modelPrediction_eq_quarter_iff hk]
  rfl

theorem dzbarAt_const_mul (c : ℂ) (F : (Fin n → ℂ) → ℂ) (j : Fin n) (z : Fin n → ℂ) :

    show ((0 : ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ) 1 + Complex.I * (0 : ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ) Complex.I) / 2 = 0
    simp
  have hslice : dbarSlice (fun x => c * F x) j z = fun t => c * dbarSlice F j z t := rfl
  show dzbar (dbarSlice (fun x => c * F x) j z) (z j) = c * dzbar (dbarSlice F j z) (z j)
  rw [hslice]
  set G := dbarSlice F j z with hG
  show wirtingerAntihol (fderiv ℝ (fun t => c * G t) (z j))
    = c * wirtingerAntihol (fderiv ℝ G (z j))
  by_cases hGd : DifferentiableAt ℝ G (z j)
  · rw [fderiv_const_mul hGd]
    show ((c • fderiv ℝ G (z j)) 1 + Complex.I * (c • fderiv ℝ G (z j)) Complex.I) / 2
      = c * ((fderiv ℝ G (z j) 1 + Complex.I * fderiv ℝ G (z j) Complex.I) / 2)
    simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    ring
  · by_cases hc0 : c = 0
    · simp [hc0, hwa0]
    · have hnd : ¬ DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun t => c * G t) (z j) := by
        intro hcon
        refine hGd ?_
        have := hcon.const_mul c⁻¹

      rw [fderiv_zero_of_not_differentiableAt hGd,
        fderiv_zero_of_not_differentiableAt hnd, hwa0, mul_zero]

/-- **`∂̄_j` is additive over a finite sum.** -/
theorem dzbarAt_finset_sum {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι)
    (F : ι → (Fin n → ℂ) → ℂ) (hF : ∀ i, Differentiable ℝ (F i)) (j : Fin n) (z : Fin n → ℂ) :
    dzbarAt (fun x => ∑ i ∈ s, F i x) j z = ∑ i ∈ s, dzbarAt (F i) j z := by
  classical
  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
  | empty =>
      simpa using dzbarAt_zero j z
  | insert a s ha ih =>
      have heq : (fun x : Fin n → ℂ => ∑ i ∈ insert a s, F i x)
          = fun x : Fin n → ℂ => F a x + ∑ i ∈ s, F i x := by
        funext x
        rw [Finset.sum_insert ha]
      have hdsum : Differentiable ℝ (fun x : Fin n → ℂ => ∑ i ∈ s, F i x) := by
        have hfun : (fun x : Fin n → ℂ => ∑ i ∈ s, F i x) = ∑ i ∈ s, F i := by
          funext x
          simp [Finset.sum_apply]
        rw [hfun]
        exact Differentiable.sum fun i _ => hF i
      rw [heq, dzbarAt_add (hF a) hdsum j z, ih, Finset.sum_insert ha]

end Linearity
